cloud.failure_mode: None. The device is BLE-local only: the app works with no account and no internet connection, and no OTA or firmware-download URLs exist in the app (only qh-tek.com privacy/about pages). Ad/analytics SDKs are bundled in the app but are not functionally required.
cloud.notes: The only vendor hosts referenced by the app are qh-tek.com (documentation pages) and the fonewe.com app-download portal; neither participates in device control.

device.name: Qianghe HappyLighting (Triones/QHM) BLE LED Strip Controller
device.notes:
Cheap BLE RGB(W) LED controllers sold under many listings and driven by the vendor "HappyLighting" app (Android and iOS). The reference instance documented here is the AliExpress 3256812708626256 4x72-LED USB car interior strip kit ("LED LAMP" / "LED Controller" inline box; its QR code resolves to the HappyLighting download portal), but the app drives the whole advertised-name family. This is the Triones / HappyLighting / QHM family — NOT Tuya and NOT the ELK-BLEDOM (duoCo) family documented in elk-bledom-led-strip.yaml; the packet formats are unrelated.
PROTOCOL: short fixed frames, no pairing, no auth, no session. Power on CC 23 33, off CC 24 33. Static color 56 R G B W F0 AA (the W byte is the white channel; the app scales it with brightness on RGBW hardware) with a variant 57 R G B W F0 75. Effect mode BB <mode> <speed> 44. Status query EF 01 77; the app parses the reply payload from byte offsets 3..9 of the notification value. A mic/music sensitivity frame 69 00 00 F0 96 is sent on the ffd5/ffd9 layout.
GATT LAYOUTS: the app supports two. Legacy units expose service 0xFFE0 with write characteristic 0xFFE1 and notify 0xFFE2. Current app builds send commands on service 0xFFD5, write characteristic 0xFFD9. Which layout a given controller revision uses could not be confirmed without hardware; try 0xFFD5/0xFFD9 first and fall back to 0xFFE0/0xFFE1. The command frames themselves are the same on both.
DISCOVERY: advertised local names matched by the app are Dream#, Dream~, Dream=, QLAMP, QHM* and Triones~ (name-contains checks, so prefixes Dream/QLAMP/QHM/Triones are the practical match).
CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM-HIGH for the command frames and both UUID sets — read straight out of the vendor app and corroborated by the community Triones documentation and Home Assistant led_ble. Which layout/name a specific unit uses, and the exact status-reply field semantics, are unverified against hardware.

credentials.notes: No auth of any kind. Physical proximity is the only access control.

factory_reset.effect: No credential or pairing state is stored on the device, so there is nothing meaningful to clear. No dedicated reset procedure is known from the app's code; power-cycling returns the controller to its default state.

steps.expect: Controller powers on in its default state and resumes advertising.

methods.description: Scan for the advertised names or service UUIDs above, connect, and write command frames to 0xFFD9 (service 0xFFD5) or 0xFFE1 (service 0xFFE0). No initialization handshake is known or needed.

steps.action: Scan for a Dream*/QLAMP/QHM*/Triones* name or the 0xFFD5 / 0xFFE0 service UUID and connect.
Write command frames to 0xFFD9 (preferred) or 0xFFE1; subscribe to 0xFFE2 on legacy-layout units for status replies.

setup.notes: No provisioning. The device advertises when powered; the vendor app connects and writes with no account, no bonding and no authentication. Confidence is medium rather than high because the flow was read from the app's code, not replayed against hardware.

rejoin.notes: No bonding and no owner binding. Any central within range can connect and take control.

testing.notes: Everything here comes from static analysis of the vendor Android app ("HappyLighting", 2026-08-19) cross-checked against the community-documented "Triones" protocol and the Home Assistant led_ble integration. No unit of this family has been driven from this spec, and no over-the-air capture exists in this project.

variants.notes: 4x rigid 5050 RGB bars (18 LEDs each, 72 total), USB 5V, inline "LED LAMP" controller whose QR code points at the HappyLighting app portal. The advertised name and GATT layout of this specific controller revision are unconfirmed — hypothesis: one of the name prefixes above with the 0xFFD5/0xFFD9 layout.

entities.name: LED Strip
entities.notes:
`set_effect` binds set_mode, which carries a speed byte alongside the mode index; a consumer that exposes only an effect list should send the speed it last used, or 0x00. The mode index table was not extracted, so the effect names have to come from the consumer, not from here.
The state binding is CONDITIONAL, and a consumer that treats it as unconditional will fail on current hardware. The app speaks two GATT layouts: legacy 0000ffe0 (write 0000ffe1, notify 0000ffe2) and current 0000ffd5, whose only documented characteristic is the write 0000ffd9 — no notify was recovered for it, so where the EF 01 77 reply lands on a current-build controller is unknown. The commands above target the current layout's write, because without them a consumer could not turn the strip on at all; state_characteristic names the legacy layout's notify, because that is the only readback anyone has documented. The two are mutually exclusive on a given unit, and which layout a controller revision speaks could not be established without hardware. So: subscribe to 0000ffe2 if discovery finds it, and drive the strip write-only if it does not — do not fail the device when the subscribe returns characteristic-not-found.

not_covered: scheduling/timers, if supported by the firmware (not extracted)
local_access.summary: Full local control over BLE as shipped: power, static color and effect modes/speed, with no account, pairing or network. Status query is the one caveat — the reply characteristic exists only on the legacy GATT layout, so readback is conditional on which layout the controller speaks (see the LED Strip entity's notes).

get_state.description: Query device status. The reply arrives as a notification (0xFFE2 on the legacy layout); the app parses state fields from byte offsets 3..9 of the value.

set_mic_sensitivity.description: Microphone/music sensitivity frame sent by the app on this layout. Fixed literal as observed; the sensitivity encoding (which byte varies) was not established.

set_mode.description: Set a dynamic effect mode and its speed. Mode indices map to the app's effect list (color jumps, fades, music-reactive patterns); the full index table was not extracted.

set_static_color.description: Set a static RGB(W) color. Byte 5 (white) is the white channel; the app scales it with brightness on RGBW hardware. Pass 0x00 for white on RGB-only strips.

set_static_color_alt.description: Alternate static-color frame emitted on a second app code path (same payload layout, 0x57 opcode, 0x75 trailer). Purpose of the variant is not established; prefer set_static_color.

characteristics.name: Write
characteristics.notes: All commands below are also accepted on 0xFFE1 of the legacy 0xFFE0 layout; the app picks the characteristic by which service the connected unit exposes.

services.name: Qianghe command service (current app builds)
services.notes: Service the current HappyLighting build writes command frames to. Frames are short fixed literals with no length prefix, no checksum and no sequence byte; each write is a complete command.

characteristics.name: Write
characteristics.notes: Write the same frames documented on 0xFFD9 (power CC 23 33 / CC 24 33, color 56 R G B W F0 AA, mode BB <mode> <speed> 44, status query EF 01 77).

characteristics.name: Notify
characteristics.notes: Status replies. The app parses the response to the EF 01 77 query from byte offsets 3..9 of the notification value; exact per-field semantics are unverified.

services.name: Qianghe legacy service
services.notes: Legacy GATT layout kept by the app for older controller revisions. Accepts the same command frames as the 0xFFD5/0xFFD9 pair.
